description: Should-trigger covers BOTH halves of this skill's two modes: planning/exploration (give me directions, explore, plan the flow, pattern choice) AND — new — ad-hoc implementation, because outside a ticketed run no other artefact owns the design quality of a UI write. The implementation query used to be labelled should-not-trigger on the reasoning that it belongs to the apply step; that step only exists as a dispatch target inside the engine, so the label routed ad-hoc implementation prompts to nobody. Should-not-trigger keeps the genuine near-misses: inventorying existing UI (existing-ui-audit owns it in both modes), a ui-trivial one-line edit, and non-UI work. Scroll-storytelling rows added 2026-08-23: a scroll-driven narrative build is an ad-hoc UI write and routes here, and the renderer axis is a third row in this skill's mode table rather than a second executor. The should-NOT-trigger row is the one that matters — "scroll position resets when I navigate back" is a state/restoration bug and belongs to the frontend-engineer lens, not to design. Without it the word "scroll" alone would route every scroll bug to a design skill.

queries.q: give me three directions for the pricing page
explore a few visual directions for the dashboard before we commit
should this filter be a modal or an inline panel?
plan the responsive layout for the settings screen
implement the selected checkout design in React exactly as approved
improve this form, it feels clunky
what form components do we already have in the codebase?
change the primary button colour to green
add a database index on orders.status
fix the failing unit test in the auth module
build the scroll-driven story section for the launch page
make the hero pin and scrub through three beats as you scroll
the scroll position resets when I navigate back — fix the restoration bug
